results.title: Battle-hardened Bosnia-Herzegovina savours underdog status in World Cup opener - The Globe and Mail
highlights:
Like Canada, the Bosnians have been sweating the health of their captain. But unlike Canada coach Jesse Marsch, Bosnian boss Sergej Barbarez had good news about his skipper’s availability for the opening match.
[...]
“Edin will be with us [on Friday], of course,” he said through an interpreter at the pregame news conference Thursday.
[...]
But Barbarez said Tabakovic, who injured his foot playing for Borussia Mönchengladbach in its Bundesliga season finale, will need more time.
[...]
“He will be, at best, joining us at the second game,” the coach said.
[...]
Dzeko, the team’s talismanic leader, has not played for his country since suffering a shoulder injury in the Italy game. The 40-year-old striker did take part in the portion of training open to the media on Thursday, however.
[...]
“We know it’s going to be a tough game,” said midfielder Stephen Eustaquio, who will captain Canada with Alphonso Davies still rehabbing his hamstring. “Bosnia’s a very experienced and a hard team to play against.”
[...]
The Bosnian players who spoke to the media Thursday said they didn’t know much about Canada’s lengthy injury list.

results.title: Scouting Report: Edin Dzeko Still Questionable Ahead Of Canada Tilt - Northern Tribune
highlights:
In what has become a mirrored storyline, both Canada’s Alphonso Davies and Bosnia-Herzegovina’s Edin Dzeko are in the final stages of physical rehabilitation while Friday’s fixture looms ever closer. At the moment, however, whether Davies or Dzeko will ultimately be fit enough to influence the match remains highly in doubt.
[...]
While Canada’s Alphonso Davies has been on a return-to-play program as Les Rouges prepare to host Bosnia and Herzegovina in downtown Toronto, the visitors saw team captain Edin Dzeko remain limited to individual training today in Etobicoke.
[...]
The 40-year-old Edin Dzeko, who suffered a shoulder injury in Bosnia and Herzegovina’s historic win over Italy, has amassed an astounding 148 caps for his country and scored 73 goals, but has only managed 64 minutes of cumulative game since since his March-time shoulder injury.
[...]
In fact, the Bosnian forward line is in a spell of trouble. Both Dzeko and forward Haris Tabakovic sat out of training today, with the duo receiving physical therapy before progressing to some individual work rather than team-based activities.
[...]
Defensive midfielder Ivan Sunjic has returned to team activities and is expected to be a starter against Canada on June 12.
[...]
Should the veteran Dzeko be sidelined for the Bosnian opener against Canada, Ermedin Demirovic is the most likely suspect to replace him. The Stuttgart forward, 28, has been Dzeko’s understudy since joining the national team in 2021, giving head coach Sergej Barbarez plenty to think about – though his track record with the national team does not reflect his strong club form.
[...]
Munich man as
[...]
With the aforementioned Haris Tabakovic still questionable as he recovers from a fractured metatarsal, the two camps have yet another mirror: it’s a case unfolding like Canada’s Moise Bombito, where it seems like the player will be given as much time to get as close to match fit as possible before a declaration of whether to keep them on the 26-man roster or name in a replacement.
[...]
Canada’s own World Cup warm-ups saw the country best Uzbekistan before finishing with a draw against Ireland, with the squad seeing Marcelo Flores replaced by left winger Jayden Nelson today. Alphonso Davies isn’t the only player on return-to-play protocol either, with Ralph Priso – another fringe replacement prospect – still on the road to full fitness, while many of Canada’s current 26-man squad having experienced their own injury issues this year.
[...]
Canada will kick off against Bosnia and Herzegovina on Friday, June 12 at 3:00PM EST.

Bosnia XI vs Canada– Predicted lineup and team news

Bosnia & Herzegovina face Canada in Toronto for a pivotal opening World Cup fixture.

Sergej Barbarez has guided his team back to the global stage after a 12-year absence. They qualified through the European playoffs after defeating both Wales and Italy on penalties. The visitors remain unbeaten in their last eight international matches across all competitions.

Advertisement

Advertisement

They boast exceptional defensive solidity, conceding very few goals during their recent unbeaten sequence. This match represents the first-ever senior meeting between the two ambitious nations. Bosnia will likely rely on compact defending and lightning-fast counter-attacks to secure a positive result.

## Bosnia-Herzegovina team news

Barbarez faces immense anxiety regarding the physical condition of captain Edin Dzeko. The legendary 40-year-old striker missed training on Tuesday with a severe shoulder injury. He remains a major doubt to start this massive Group B clash.

Dzeko represents his nation’s all-time top scorer and central tactical focal point. Striker Haris Tabakovic is also highly unlikely to play following a late-season ankle issue.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Ermedin Demirovic will shoulder the attacking responsibility if Dzeko fails his late fitness test. PSV star Esmir Bajraktarevic will provide unpredictable creative quality from the flanks. Benjamin Tahirovic and Armin Gigovic will anchor the midfield to protect the defensive line.

Sead Kolasinac brings invaluable experience to a youthful and energetic defensive unit. Nikola Katic enters the match full of confidence after recently scoring against Panama.

## Bosnia-Herzegovina predicted lineup

Bosnia-Herzegovina predicted XI: Vasilj; Burnic, Gigovic, Muharemovic, Memic; Celik, Basic, Bajraktarevic; Mahmic, Demirovic, Bazdar.

results.title: Barbarez: Dzeko will most likely not play against Panama - Sarajevo Times
highlights:
Barbarez: Dzeko will most likely not play against Panama - Sarajevo Times
[...]
At the Energizer Park stadium in St. Louis was given an official training session by the BiH national team before the match with Panama.
[...]
Before the start of the training, a press conference of our team was held, where the selector Sergej Barbarez and the national team member Nidal Čelik answered questions from journalists, reports the official website of the Football Association of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
[...]
Barbarez also referred to the health bulletin, pointing out that Edin Džeko and Ivan Šunjić will not play in that match, the media reports.
[...]
“As for Edin, he will most likely not be in the team tomorrow at all because we haven’t fully resolved his injury. He still has a few problems and that’s why we decided that he will be spared today, and simply take him out of the training process for a few days to focus on the match in Canada. Ivan Šunjić is the only one still out with him, but there won’t be any problems going forward. He is almost at the level and is starting to train with us,” Barbarez said, according to the media.
[...]
We are all ready for what awaits us at the World Cup, but right now we are only focused on tomorrow’s match with Panama, Čelik said.
[...]
The Panama-Bosnia and Herzegovina match is scheduled for today, June 6 at 2:00 PM local time (9:00 PM CET) at Energizer Park in St. Louis.
